basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the Spanish retail market and, if so, how?

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess the size, competition and buyer needs of the Spanish retail market and Quinta Azul's capability to win there.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Compare entry options for Spain, build the business case and draft the entry roadmap for the go or no-go.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?

workstreams.name: Spain retail attractiveness
workstreams.answers: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
activities: Size Spanish retail demand and growth by segment
Map retail channels and regulation affecting olive oil
Rate segment attractiveness for Quinta Azul's oil

workstreams.name: Competitors and buyer needs
workstreams.answers: Who competes in Spanish retail olive oil, and what do retail buyers and shoppers there need?
activities: Profile competitors and their position in Spanish retail
Interview Spanish retail buyers on what they look for
Collect shopper views on how they choose olive oil

workstreams.name: Capability to win in Spain
workstreams.answers: Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spanish retail?
activities: Interview leaders and the people who do the work
Review operational data and documents on current assets
Assess gaps between assets and what winning in Spain takes

workstreams.name: Entry options for Spain
workstreams.answers: Which entry options exist for Quinta Azul in Spain, and how do they compare on agreed criteria?
activities: Identify entry options for selling in Spanish retail
Agree comparison criteria with Quinta Azul's leaders
Compare options on the agreed criteria

workstreams.name: Spain business case
workstreams.answers: Does the business case for the preferred entry option support a go or no-go on Spain?
activities: Build a business case for the preferred entry option
Model costs, revenue and risks of the option in Spain
Test the business case against the go or no-go question

workstreams.name: Spain entry roadmap
workstreams.answers: If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow in Spain?
activities: Sequence the steps to enter Spanish retail
Draft the entry plan and roadmap for approval

deliverables.name: Spanish retail market size and segment attractiveness
Competitor profiles for Spanish retail olive oil
Spanish retail buyer and shopper needs findings
Gap assessment of Quinta Azul's assets for Spain
Spain attractiveness findings pack for sign-off
Entry options for Spain compared on agreed criteria
Business case for the preferred entry option
Entry plan and roadmap for Spanish retail
Go or no-go decision pack for Spain

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Launch Research and secure data access
events.decision: Which Quinta Azul sales data and buyer contacts can the team access?
agenda: Present the Spain entry question and the Research workstreams
Discuss the data and people the evidence work needs
Align on owners and dates for each access request

events.label: Check-in: first findings
events.purpose: Review market size and competitor findings
events.decision: Which retail segments should the findings pack take to sign-off?
agenda: Present the Spanish retail market size by segment
Review competitor profiles for Spanish retail olive oil
Discuss which segments the findings pack should carry

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.purpose: Decide whether Spain justifies entry design
events.decision: Is Spain attractive enough to justify designing entry options?
agenda: Present the Spain attractiveness findings pack
Review the competitor, buyer and capability findings behind it
Decide whether to move on to entry option design

events.label: Check-in: entry options
events.purpose: Review entry options before the roadmap
events.decision: Which entry option should the roadmap and go or no-go pack detail?
agenda: Present the entry options compared on agreed criteria
Review how the options differ against the criteria
Discuss which option the roadmap and go or no-go pack detail

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision
events.decision: Approve the Spain go or no-go decision and, if go, the entry plan?
agenda: Present the go or no-go decision pack and the business case
Review the entry plan and roadmap for Spanish retail
Decide on the go or no-go and, if go, the entry plan

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so the 7 to 10 weeks are an estimate from the sizing; confirm length and any deadline before quoting.
Design is sized for a go outcome; a no-go would drop the entry roadmap and shorten the phase.

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is the Spanish retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Who competes there, and what do Spanish retail buyers and shoppers need?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in Spain?
Which entry options exist for Spain, and does the business case support a go or no-go?
If the answer is go, what entry plan and roadmap should Quinta Azul follow?

phases.name: Research

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phases.why: Spain is assessed as one market in full; the capability check and leadership interviews run alongside it.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phases.why: The entry option and business case for Spain come first, then the entry roadmap, one after the other.

sizing.levers: Assessing only the retail channels the CEO and Commercial Director prioritize, and starting the roadmap alongside the business case, would shorten the engagement most.
